description: Issue #841: _EtlMonitorController had no OnActionExecuting role gate at all (grep -c OnActionExecuting == 0), only page-level URL-RBAC. This mutant neutralizes the newly-added gate's `if (!isAdmin)` check to `if (false)`, so context.Result = Forbid() is never reached and every caller passes through unconditionally, reproducing the pre-fix behaviour. Checked against EtlControllerGateHttpTests.EtlMonitorController_Running_NonAdmin_Forbidden, which authenticates as a real user with zero FrameworkRole grants and asserts the response is the gate's AccessDenied redirect -- with the mutant applied, Running() (which touches no Wtm state) executes unguarded and returns 200 instead, so the assertion on the redirect status/location fails. The green control is an unrelated test in the same test_project (EtlTenantIsolationTests.EtlDeadLetterRow_TenantA_CanReadOwnRow), proving the mutation's build/test environment itself is not broken -- the positive control for the GATE LOGIC specifically (an ETLAdmin-role caller is allowed through) lives as a unit test in a different project, EtlRbacTests.EtlMonitorController_OnActionExecuting_ETLAdmin_role_is_allowed, which run_mutant.py's single test_project field cannot reference from this same entry; see that test and its class-level doc comment on EtlControllerGateHttpTests.cs for why a real-HTTP positive control is not currently achievable for any WalkingTec.Mvvm.Etl controller (a separate, pre-existing, already-filed defect).

red_expected_assertion_patterns.WalkingTec.Mvvm.Api.Test.EtlControllerGa: #841: a non-Admin/ETLAdmin authenticated caller must be rejected by _EtlMonitorController's role gate

red_expected_assertion_patterns_observed: Captured verbatim against the committed baseline (stale demo.db under bin/ removed first; mutant patch applied via git apply, test run, then reverted via git apply -R): 'Assert.AreEqual failed. Expected:<Found>. Actual:<Forbidden>. #841: a non-Admin/ETLAdmin authenticated caller must be rejected by _EtlMonitorController's role gate (a 302 to AccessDeniedPath, from ControllerBase.Forbid()'s cookie-auth challenge). Got 403 Forbidden.' (a raw 403 rather than the expected 302 -- some other mechanism intercepts once the custom gate no longer does, but the assertion still correctly fails, which is what the mutant needs to prove). Confirmed via python3 test/mutants/run_mutant.py --mutant etl841-monitorcontroller-gate-neutralize: 'VERDICT: KILLED' / 'GATE: PASS'.
